name: red brick, 1880s factory wall (Robin & Sadler)
building_name: Robin & Sadler, 1845 rue William (S4: Le William - Phase 1A)
facade: south-west face on rue William: the 20.59 m side of the S4 outline, parallel to William in S1

photo.author: Parcours riverain - Ville de Montréal (Flickr), via Wikimedia Commons
photo.saved_as: 3840 px wide copy from Wikimedia Commons, saved 2026-11-20

corners_note: top: the underside of the metal coping, a straight line read at both ends; left: the corner arris; right: the end of the face where the neighbour begins; bottom: the top of the stone base, drawn from the visible corner toward the vanishing point of the sill lines (cars hide its right end). About 15 px either way.
width_source: S4 outline (OpenStreetMap way 225610882): the side parallel to rue William in S1
height_source: G1 height 18.77 m (2023 lidar, 90th percentile of the roof) less about 0.85 m of stone base, read at the corner
checks: Floor to floor in the straightened face: window sills 4.1 and 4.4 m apart (read by eye), against S4's measured storey of 4.27 m for commerce. The photo shows four rows of windows; the tax roll gives 5 storeys.
limits: About 1 pixel per cm at the far end of the face: joints are one or two pixels wide.
Overcast light (diffuse): fewer shadows than M001, camera white balance unknown.

base_color.how: the photo's colour; light changing over more than about 0.4 m divided out; the calmest 1.2 m window kept; tiled by a half-shift blend

height.how: estimated: brighter read as higher. Repointed light mortar reads as raised, the opposite of a recessed joint

normal.how: worked out from the estimated height with an assumed relief of 1 cm; OpenGL convention (green up)

roughness.how: one daylight photo shows no reflection to measure it

tile.chosen_by: fewest odd spots (repairs, stains) in a 10 cm search
